COHERENT SINGLE-SHOT MEMORY — FROZEN CORRECTIONS AND AUDIT RECONCILIATION
9 October 2026. Append-only v2; v1 remains unchanged.

This version supersedes the CSS contraction and AKP conversion constants in v1.
It also states the coherent-controller argument in a representation that does
not assume nonlinear Boolean gates preserve Pauli errors. The theorem in v1
remains the candidate theorem with the corrected constants below. Independent
audits support its algebra and encoded-input good-path quantifier. They are
internal examinations, not external verification or novelty validation.

1. CSS FACTOR TWO (SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTION)

Let alpha0 be the contraction constant of each SOURCE X/Z decoder. Choose a
fixed number of QTC parallel iterations so alpha0<1/2, and put alpha=2 alpha0<1.
Keep r=the TOTAL stabilizer-reduced Pauli weight used by v1 (not the sum of
separately minimized component weights). If e has a representative X(x)Z(z) of
weight r, then |x|_red<=r and |z|_red<=r, so |x|_red+|z|_red<=2r. Consequently

 |e+f_X+f_Z|_red <= alpha0(|x|_red+|z|_red)+beta(|D_X|_V+|D_Z|_V)
                    <= alpha r+beta |D|_V,

where beta is the maximum component beta and |D|_V denotes the summed component
syndrome support. a_ext,b_ext include both extraction blocks and b_ext bounds
this sum. A,B,h can be safely chosen to satisfy both component premises whenever
A r+B |D|_V<=h n. Hence all v1 equations (3)-(21) hold with effective alpha=2alpha0.
The sentence in v1 Section1 asserting 'the same alpha' from component weights
<=r was incorrect. For the logical CNOT extension in v3, choose alpha0<1/4 so
this effective alpha is below 1/2.

2. AKP HAMILTONIAN CONSTANT (SUBSTANTIVE SOURCE CORRECTION)

The correct constant in AKP arXiv:quant-ph/0510231v1, Eq22 and Eq24, is

  C_A=exp(1+1/(2e)),  eta_noise=C_A sqrt(2 mu),

not exp(1-1/(2e)) as written in v1 and imported from A04's initial source audit.
The primary published PDF also prints the plus sign at Eq24, page4; live web
text lines364-367 of https://preskill.caltech.edu/pubs/preskill-2006-long-range.pdf
were checked. Thus v1 Section7's sufficient row-norm bound must use

  mu <= eta0^2/[2 exp(2+1/e)],  eta0=tau/(e^3 N0).

Positivity and all asymptotic memory conclusions survive. The numerical cutoff
is smaller. No empirical calibration claim is attached to this source result.

PROTECTED ENTANGLING OPERATIONS AND ENCODED TRANSFER UNDER ONE COHERENT BATH
9 October 2026. Frozen v3. Extends the corrected memory theorem in v1+v2.

STATUS: internally derived operational extension, not external validation or a
new universal quantum computer. The physical CNOT and encoded-transfer circuits
below are actually executed with all their faults counted. No ideal final
decoder is executed inside these primitives. Ideal final decoding continues to
define their logical error metric, as is standard for encoded output. A bare
quantum output immune to its last allowed fault is impossible in this model.

1. EXACT NATIVE ENTANGLING GATE

Write a CSS code using binary subspaces A (X stabilizers) and B (Z stabilizers),
with A subset B^perp, and select a linear section of the quotient B^perp/A.
For u in that section, its logical computational basis is

 |[u]> = |A|^(-1/2) sum_{a in A} |u+a>.

Apply CNOT to every corresponding physical pair of two identical code blocks.
For u,v,

 CNOT^tensor n |[u]>|[v]>
 = |A|^(-1) sum_{a,b in A}|u+a>|u+v+a+b>
 = |[u]>|[u+v]>.

Thus the circuit implements all k corresponding logical CNOTs simultaneously.
Its entangling gates have depth1 and n two-qubit locations. This is a known CSS
transversal property, reconstructed here to specify exact logical addressing.
It does not implement a CNOT between arbitrary independently chosen indices
inside the blocks. A prescribed sequence of block-matching CNOTs is supported.

If a Pauli before the CNOT is X(a)Z(b) on source and X(c)Z(d) on target, propagation
gives X(a)Z(b+d) on source and X(a+c)Z(d) on target, up to phase. For reduced
weights r_A,r_B, choose minimal representatives first; each propagated block
has reduced weight at most r_A+r_B. Clifford covariance removes no information
from a shared bath and does not require stochastic paths.

2. COMPLETELY LOCAL ENCODED TRANSFER WITH NOISY READOUT/FEEDFORWARD

Input source block A contains arbitrary unknown encoded |psi> (possibly entangled
with other logical blocks or a reference). Input target block B is a SUPPLIED
or preexisting protected |[0]> state of the same CSS code. Run:

 (i) corresponding-qubit transversal CNOT A->B;
 (ii) X-measure every source physical qubit, obtaining the n-bit string x;
 (iii) apply physical Z(x)=product_i Z_i^(x_i) to target, using one local

EXACT COMPATIBILITY WITH THE INTRINSIC LOCAL-CHART qLTC DECODER
9 October 2026. Frozen v4; independent QTC theorem v1-v3 unchanged.

This is a dependency-preserving application of the complete coherent-recovery
construction, not an independent validation of the GGJ code family or Sol6's
new decoder. The source family and decoder proof retain their own hypotheses
and audit status. It identifies an actual compatible consequence beyond a
mere analogy between local charts and quantum fault tolerance.

1. INPUT THEOREM INSPECTED

Read work/sol/local_chart_decoder/v1.txt and v2.txt. The operative statement is
v2 Eq(5.4): for every fixed desired physical alpha in (0,1), its binary CSS
decoder f has constants beta_phys,eta_data,eta_syndrome>0 independent of N,

 |e+f(syn(e)+m)|_physical,stab-red
     <= alpha |e|_physical,stab-red + beta_phys |m|_bits,

provided |e|_physical,stab-red<=eta_data N and |m|_bits<=eta_syndrome N.
The entire decoder, including the actual-stalk transpose reduction, has O(N)
Boolean gates, constant depth and bounded fanout at fixed source parameters.
Its local neighborhoods are fixed stars; finite field, stalk dimensions,
local matrices, cube ladder height, local splittings and trace-dual binary
conversions are fixed as the family index grows. Preprocessing/coloring and
the code description are supplied/hardwired before repeated operation.

The source-reported GGJ family has k_N>=R N, d_N>=d0 N, fixed check/qubit degree
and constant-size check support. These remain GGJ dependencies, not discoveries
made by this application. Sol6 already absorbs the two CSS components and their
block-to-bit inflation into its PHYSICAL alpha; unlike QTC source alpha0, no
further factor2 should be inserted silently. Select its desired physical alpha
directly for the required spread constant.

2. COUNTED PHYSICAL COMPILATION

Constant-weight bounded-degree check extraction is edge-colored as in v1.
Every local finite-field/binary operation and gain choice in the decoder is a
fixed finite truth table. Purify it reversibly and implement with a fixed number
of elementary one/two-qubit/control operations. Code-star incidence links,
readout, idles, scratch resets, messages and physical Pauli corrections are
all counted. Bounded depth/fanout implies each marked decoder location changes
